name: plangate-session-only-binds
description:
A session-only slot binds and the permissioned call SUCCEEDS with NO standing tuple existing anywhere — no `owner` relationship on reposcope_repo, no SpiceDBBootstrap granting anything (see 00-agent.yaml: this fixture ships none). reposcope_repo declares no `standing`, so it resolves to the CRD default (session-only): the approver's decision on the plan-gate card IS the authority. That is the case that was impossible before this feature — previously the approver-standing pre-check asked SpiceDB whether the approver already held `push` on the named repository, which nobody upstream-governed ever does.

Session-only is not 'no gate': the plan gate still requires an approved phase, the slot still binds to the NAMED instance, the grant is still written with a mandatory expiry and is still session-scoped and revocable, and the tool-call Check still resolves slot_grant_push->interact + owner. The only thing skipped is the pre-check.

The push tool is called TWICE in the same session after ONE approval. approvalPrompts:1 is what distinguishes a persisted grant from one re-granted per call — the exact gap that let a missing decision-writer sit behind a green scenario before. Both calls are asserted on the TOOL RESULT, not the reply, because a scripted transcript says the same words whether the call returned success or a permission error.

The card copy is asserted too, since this feature changes what a human reads: the session-only sentence must appear, and no internal vocabulary (slot_grant, the escaped object id, SpiceDB/agentsession terms) may leak onto it.

All of it sits in ONE user turn deliberately, matching every other plangate-* bundle. Each turn boundary is a race: after agent_work_complete the runner makes one more model call, and whether the next user message has landed by then decides what that call carries. Fewer boundaries, fewer ways for a positional transcript to drift.
